A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRC image-watermarking work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-quality, detectability, robustness and message-decoding experiments, plus the VAE demonstration in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds classifier-architecture and randomized-key detectability experiments in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The PRC construction, latent sampling, inversion, soft-decision detection and message decoding remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–8. The additional classifiers are evaluation models.

E1.justification: Figure 7 adds detection scenarios where baseline watermarked images use randomly selected keys from pools of two or ten. This differs from v2's fixed-key detection and classification between two specific keys. Dataset and domain coverage otherwise remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The competing watermark schemes and their membership in retained comparisons are unchanged. New Figure 7 reuses Tree-Ring, Gaussian Shading and StegaStamp from Figure 2; Figure 6 varies classifiers probing PRC rather than introducing competing watermark schemes.

E3.justification: New Figure 6 evaluates ResNet50, ResNet101, AlexNet and VGG19 alongside ResNet18. Figure 7 introduces ResNet18 evaluations with two-key and ten-key mixtures. These are additional evaluation conditions; the documented settings of retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 6–7 add checks of whether PRC detectability depends on classifier architecture and whether mixing baseline watermark keys prevents learned detection. Existing attack, sparsity, decoder-robustness and message-capacity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly highlights scores outside three standard errors in red and states this criterion in its caption. Existing means, standard errors and aggregation procedures remain unchanged; no additional runs or seeds are documented.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds near-chance PRC validation results across five classifier architectures. Figure 7 shows Tree-Ring, Gaussian Shading and StegaStamp remain detectable with randomized key mixtures. Figure 1 replaces five post-processing example outputs. Tables 1–2 and the retained quantitative plots have unchanged results.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, Theorems 1–2, detector derivation and appendix proofs are unchanged. The decoder false-positive bound appearing earlier in v3 was already present across the page break in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about undetectability, quality preservation, robustness and message capacity. The additional experiments support existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, robustness–security tradeoffs and practical-undetectability limitations remain unchanged, including Appendix C.3. The added captions report experimental findings without introducing new mechanism arguments or limitations.

D1.justification: Documentation accompanying the new analyses identifies the classifier architectures and specifies generating each mixed-key sample after randomly selecting a key. Existing pseudocode, hardware, implementation hyperparameters, dependencies and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to Tree-Ring, Gaussian Shading and earlier pseudorandom-code constructions are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates the publication header and author-contact formatting, removes the acknowledgements, and updates appendix figure listings and cross-references. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 replaces five image panels in Figure 1, adds Figures 6–7 and introduces red highlighting in Table 1. Existing appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, including the decoder comparison moving from Figure 11 to Figure 10.

improvement.justification: Figures 6–7 modestly strengthen the empirical detectability comparison by testing additional classifiers and randomized baseline keys. Table 1 also makes its uncertainty-based highlighting explicit. A drawback is that Figure 1 replaces matched post-processing examples with different scenes while retaining its original caption, weakening the visual comparison. The added quantitative checks provide a limited net improvement despite this presentation problem.
